Ask the production instances which names REDCap knows

round_known_names.Rd

Decided on 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-12 (item 4 (b') of the 0.26.0): before a verdict that can make an account, the round asks every production instance which of the names it could create REDCap already knows. Known means a row in redcap_user_information, which accounts reads (module_accounts(), through report_server_reads()), or a row in redcap_user_rights, which the whole-instance read of state carries: measured on 2026-11-12, seven productions out of eight hold names with rights and no account, people added to a project before their first sign-in.

Usage

round_known_names(usernames, productions, hosts, secrets)

Arguments

usernames

The names to ask, as the round would create them.

productions

The names of the production instances, keys of hosts.

hosts, secrets

As provisioning_reconcile() receives them.

Value

A list with asked, the names asked of every production (empty when one was not read), known, the names REDCap knows on any of them, folded as identity_normalize() folds them, and errors, the reason of each production not read, once per code.

Details

An instance is read only when both answer. StateReader::read() answers an empty list when its query fails, so a production with no pair at all is an instance not read, TRASPORTO_STATO_VUOTO, and not one where nobody has rights. With any production not read the round has asked nothing: asked is empty and no name is verified, the direction that does not create. The state read is skipped on an instance whose accounts failed, so a machine switched off costs one wait and not two.

The benches are not asked, switched on or off (they hold no real people); the caller leaves them out of productions. With no production at all there is nobody to ask and every name is verified.
